title: Smooth stacking & scroll stability for dashboards, charts, and modals
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Scope: polish and harden the Console surface to prevent layout jank and inconsistent stacking/scroll behavior across dashboards, rollout panels, cost tables, chart canvases, and modal overlays. This ticket covers design prototypes, chrome/safari/firefox-specific workarounds, accessibility edge-cases, and a clear handoff for engineering with visual QA steps.

Goals:
- Eliminate transient layout shifts during dynamic content load (charts, streaming cost rows) for top-level dashboards.
- Ensure modal stacking and focus management is deterministic when multiple overlays are opened (rollout preview -> confirm modal -> helper tooltip).
- Make sticky headers and column-virtualization play nicely with anchored scroll positions and keyboard navigation.
- Resolve cross-browser inconsistencies (Safari zoom/overflow, Firefox scroll anchoring, Chrome overscroll bounce on macOS/iOS).
- Keep visual diffs within acceptable thresholds and keep CLS regression < 0.05 on sample workloads.

Design proposals (what to build):
1) Stacking context model: define z-index scale and out-of-flow container pattern. Provide Figma tokens for top-level surfaces (base, overlay, modal, toast, tooltip) and annotate focus traps.
2) Scroll anchoring rules: when charts or table rows appear above current viewport (e.g., streaming billing rows), pin content via explicit placeholders or use reserved height skeletons to avoid reflow.
3) Modal layering UX: modal children open into a single overlay layer with internal stacking and arbitration rules (ESC closes last, backdrop click closes last). Add a compact breadcrumb header for stacked modals to show context.
4) Sticky headers + virtualization: switch from absolute positioning to transform-based sticky when virtualization is enabled to reduce repaints and preserve scroll offsets.
5) Chart canvas fallback: ensure chart reflows do not push content unexpectedly; use reserved canvas height and a progressive reveal animation that does not change layout flow.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype (Figma) approved by PM and Eng and linked in ticket.
- Engineering PR with implementation link (see Comments) and a passing visual regression suite (Percy/Goldens) covering 6 breakpoints and 7 browsers.
- Measured CLS < 0.05 and first input delay (FID) within current console targets for affected pages.
- Keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements verified for stacked modals and sticky headers.
- QA checklist filled and cross-browser bugs triaged or resolved.

Artifacts / references:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD_CONSOLE/stacking-scroll-stability-proto (private)
- Design brief / goals: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/564321/Stacking+and+Scroll+Stability+Design+Brief
- Engineering PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8342
- Visual regression dashboard: https://percy.io/redwood/console/changes?query=DES-75931
- Performance dashboard (sample runs): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/scroll-stability/console-jank

Notes on cross-browser quirks we investigated:
- Safari: content zoom + elastic overscroll causes occasional layout jumps on iOS when restoring scroll position after opening a modal. Mitigation: apply -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch carefully, add reserved space for native bounce, and detect iOS to apply a small top padding in the overlay container.
- Firefox: scroll anchoring and focus restoration can change scrollTop unexpectedly when DOM nodes are inserted. Mitigation: insert placeholders before network data arrives; defer focus restoration until layout stabilizes.
- Chrome (macOS): transform-based sticky headers reduce repaint cost; avoid using position: sticky where virtualization library manipulates transforms.

Accessibility & edge cases:
- Ensure focus trap is maintained for stacked overlays. Use aria-hidden toggles on background portals to satisfy screen readers.
- Provide announcements for dynamic content insertion (aria-live polite) for streaming cost rows so SR users are aware without changing focus.
- Validate keyboard-only flow: open rollout panel -> open confirm modal -> close via ESC/backdrop -> ensure focus returns to original trigger.

Handoff for engineers (deliverables):
- Figma token export (z-index scale, overlay paddings, reserved heights).
- Detailed dev notes in Confluence with code snippets for placeholder strategy and virtualization switch.
- Visual test spec (Percy scenarios + breakpoints).

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Reserving fixed heights reduces jank but may increase perceived whitespace for some datasets; will surface in usability testing.
- Workarounds for iOS elastic overscroll are inherently platform-specific and require careful platform detection; need e2e tests on device lab.

Next steps:
- Finalize prototype and get PM sign-off (due 2026-03-18).
- Sync with ENG (runtime and frontend leads) on virtualization implications (meeting scheduled 2026-03-12).
- Hand off tokens and visual spec after iteration based on engineering feedback.
